correctness.rationale: The graph used is the anticommutation graph exactly C_(2k+1), k≥2. A label dependency lies in the kernel of its binary adjacency matrix; the kernel equation forces a two-periodic, thus constant, vector. No proper subset has a dependency. Independently of the cited projected-polytope theorem, a commuting independent set with assigned signs gives a normalized common-eigenspace projector. Expanding this projector into Pauli products gives zero expectation on every measured observable outside the set, since none of those labels is in the span; completing the commuting subgroup expresses the projector as a stabilizer mixture. In the other direction, a pure stabilizer projection has ±1 support on a commuting subset and zero elsewhere. Thus the polytope is the unconditional lift of STAB(C). The edge and odd-hole inequalities suffice: on a zero coordinate face the remaining path polytope is integral and its k disjoint edges imply the sum bound; with all coordinates positive, a vertex would require all or all but one edge equation. All edges tight gives the forbidden all-half vector; all but one plus the sum equation forces a coordinate to zero. For the centrally symmetric lift, the signed-affine norm is max(1,gauge), by splitting a convex representation of b/gauge into oppositely signed contributions at opposite points. An edge has capacity sqrt(2) by anticommutation. For the odd-hole term maximize signed Hamiltonian top eigenvalues. On each eigenspace of the central involution i∏P_j, monomials from a symplectic basis of the rank-2k quotient form k standard Pauli pairs. They generate M_(2^k) with a multiplicity factor; the remaining cycle product is fixed by the central sign. Matching these pairs and the center to the Majorana realization (flipping one generator as needed) covers arbitrary realizations. Edge-sign switching of the skew adjacency leaves just a flux; negating all signs flips the flux for odd length and preserves positive singular modes. The all-plus skew spectrum 2i sin(2πj/L) gives the largest energy 2∑_(j=1)^k sin(2πj/L)=cot(π/(2L)), with mode occupancies chosen independently. Dividing by k and comparing to sqrt(2) gives the stated maximum. Strict concavity of x↦cot(π/(4x+2)) from zero makes its ratio to x strictly decreasing. The exact k=4 and k=5 comparisons straddle sqrt(2), as claimed. Eigenstates attain both constituent optima where needed.
residual_risks: Scope is measurement-projected signed-affine robustness, not full-state robustness. Finite spectral and LP tests are not all-length or all-realization certificates; the proof is analytic.

evidence: Varela et al. give the general consistent-sign projection. Liu et al. reduce to the sign-relaxed polytope absent active dependencies, with explicit clique capacity for perfect graphs. Xu et al. describe the odd-hole facets; Chapman et al. give general free-fermion line-graph solvability. The later compatibility proposition is graph-general.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The earlier perfect-graph closed formula cannot be specialized to C_L for odd L≥5, and it actually misses the term that dominates at C5/C7/C9. General projections and a separate spectrum do not by themselves compare the edge and odd-hole witness strengths. The later broader gauge does apply once the cycle's projected polytope is identified.

evidence: Earlier results supply the signed-vertex model, the classical odd-cycle constraints and the cycle support separately. For this cycle one must exclude active dependencies in every realization, turn the signed-affine problem into a dilation gauge, take each facet support over quantum states, and compare the edge to the hole. The later gauge/support framework performs the main link generically.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: With that later framework the answer follows by inserting the edge and odd-cycle inequalities of STAB(C_L), whose supports are sqrt(2) and Lη(C_L), respectively, then dividing the latter by k and checking the crossing. This is an actual implication, not a claim that the later work must print the exact expression. The earlier literature inspected does not give that combined reduced-magic statement as the specialization of a single stronger theorem. The supported contribution is the cycle-specific synthesis and witness transition, not a new method for computing skew energy.

evidence: McNulty's η(C_L)=cot(π/(2L))/L is the uniform incompatibility optimum; the edge-transitive line-graph calculation yields the normalized uniform signed-Hamiltonian support. McNulty–Facchi–Pascazio identify Adv(G)=max_ρ R_G(ρ), where R_G is the least dilation of STAB(G) containing the absolute profile of ρ.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: For these cycles there is no active dependency, hence that later seed gauge is the same reduced RoM pointwise, not a merely similar monotone. Maximizing it over states gives the same capacity. The earlier uniform incompatibility value only supplies the normalized odd-hole support, not the maximum over the allowed witness types.

originality.rationale: Supported for the specific all-odd-cycle reduced-magic synthesis and sharp C11 crossover, not for the projected-polytope framework, odd-cycle facets, or all-length cotangent spectrum in isolation. An important omission in the frozen literature discussion is McNulty's preceding exact cycle incompatibility result, not merely a general free-fermion method. It already contains the normalized cycle support that supplies the spectral ingredient. The earlier reduced-magic theorem gives the clique rule for perfect graphs and does not settle how the odd-hole inequality competes with it on imperfect graphs. A later compatibility paper supplies an equivalent gauge on these cycles and, together with the cycle facets, covers the same capacity as a corollary; this is substantive equivalent coverage but not evidence the frozen statement was preceded by that paper.
residual_risks: The two closest incompatibility comparisons should be credited alongside the frozen citations; the earlier spectrum is not new, and the later gauge gives a mathematically equivalent formulation for these cycles.
No absolute priority is certified. A differently indexed earlier combination of these ingredients was not ruled out exhaustively.

value.rationale: Odd cycles are a basic nonperfect test family for the reduced stabilizer method. Imperfection produces a necessary additional facet but does not imply an increase in maximal reduced magic over an edge: the theorem pinpoints exactly when the genuinely nonclique witness improves capacity and when it remains only a pointwise distinction. That finite crossover and the all-realization exact certificate are useful benchmarks beyond the previous perfect-graph rule, not a recomputation of the known quadratic spectrum as an end in itself.
residual_risks: The comparison is specific to the stipulated observables; there is no claimed gain for full-state magic or arbitrary imperfect graphs.
